description: Tests whether the comp-modeling skill activates when it should and stays quiet when it shouldn't.

evals.prompt: I have data from a 2-armed bandit task with 30 subjects and 200 trials each. I want to estimate a learning rate per subject. What should I do?
must_include: mention of simulation or parameter recovery before fitting
recommendation to compare against a baseline / alternative model
hBayesDM mentioned OR a clear Stan/Python implementation path
softmax / Rescorla-Wagner / Q-learning named
must_not_include: going straight to a fit without mentioning recovery or PPC

evals.prompt: Help me fit prospect theory to choices on a mixed-gambles task.
must_include: loss aversion lambda parameter discussed
value-function curvature parameter (alpha) discussed
recommendation to compare against expected utility as baseline
Sokol-Hessner mentioned OR hBayesDM ra_prospect mentioned OR equivalent toolbox

evals.prompt: I want to fit a drift diffusion model to my perceptual decision-making RTs. What parameters should I estimate?
must_include: drift rate v explained
boundary separation a explained
non-decision time t explained
starting point z mentioned
HDDM mentioned
warning about RT units (seconds vs ms) OR about preprocessing

evals.prompt: How do I fit Nosofsky's GCM to a categorization dataset?
must_include: exemplar representation explained
similarity function exp(-c * distance) form
attention weights w_k mentioned
Minkowski-r distance (city-block vs Euclidean) discussed
catlearn or BayesGCM mentioned as a toolbox

evals.prompt: I have intertemporal choice data with delays from 1 day to 1 year. Fit a discount rate per subject.
must_include: hyperbolic and exponential both named (with hyperbolic as default empirical winner)
log scale for k mentioned
comparison between at least two discount functions recommended
hBayesDM dd_* family OR Vincent 2016 mentioned
must_not_include: claim that linear-scale k fitting is fine

evals.prompt: I'm running a restless 4-armed bandit a la Daw et al. 2006. Do I need anything more than Rescorla-Wagner?
must_include: Kalman filter mentioned as the standard model for this paradigm
directed exploration / uncertainty bonus mentioned
comparison with RW still recommended

evals.prompt: I want to estimate trial-by-trial learning rates that adapt to environmental volatility. What model captures this?
must_include: Behrens 2007 volatility model OR HGF (Mathys et al.) mentioned
Kalman filter mentioned as a simpler related option
warning about parameter recovery for HGF / mention of TAPAS

evals.prompt: I have some choice data and want to get a learning rate out of it
must_include: asks for or clarifies task structure (bandit? reversal? trials per subject?)
mentions the simulate -> recover -> fit -> compare workflow at least in outline

evals.prompt: I have a tabular dataset and want to predict customer churn. What model should I use?
must_include: recommends predictive ML approach (logistic regression, gradient boosting, etc.)
must_not_include: mentions parameter recovery in the cognitive-modeling sense
treats this as a cognitive modeling problem

evals.prompt: I want to run an ANOVA on accuracy across three conditions.
must_include: discusses ANOVA or appropriate alternative (mixed model)
must_not_include: talks about likelihood functions for trial-level behavior

evals.prompt: How do I train a transformer for sentiment analysis?
must_not_include: talks about learning rates as cognitive parameters

evals.prompt: I want the mean and SD of RT in each condition.
I'm fitting a model with softmax outputs to behavioral choices. The learning rate isn't converging.
must_include: asks clarifying question to determine if this is a cognitive model (RW + softmax) or a neural network being fit to behavior
OR provides guidance covering both interpretations
must_not_include: assumes it's a neural net without checking
